name: Lang Co
provinceNote: Later official pages print xã Chân Mây - Lăng Cô, thành phố Huế. The 2018 decision and the national beach page still print Thừa Thiên Huế.
dotReason: Worth a night if this bay is the picture you came for
summary: A beach town on a long sandy strip under the Hai Van Pass, between Hue and Da Nang. Swim in the clear water of the bay, watch the boats on Lap An lagoon, drive up to the Hai Van gate, and eat local oysters cooked many ways. One night suits travellers who want a quiet beach stop on the coast road.
timeNeeded: One night if the bay is the trip
getThere: About 60 km south of Hue, or about 25 km from Da Nang through the Hai Van tunnel. Minutes are check on arrival.
seoTitle: Lang Co travel guide — the bay under Hai Van, lagoon oysters
seoDescription: The bay under the Hai Van ridge, and oysters on Lap An. Hue is about 60 km north. Da Nang is about 25 km through the tunnel.
intro: You wake to the curve of the bay under the Hai Van ridge, and the lagoon is on the other side of the same strip. Stay if that morning is the trip. Go to Hue if you wanted the citadel, and to Da Nang if you wanted the city beach.

Swim and walk in the morning and late afternoon, while the ridge is still in the light. The national beach page describes about 10 km of gentle shore, white sand, and clear water, and it does not print a beach ticket. The 25 km figure from Da Nang is through the road tunnel, on that page only. The pass road is the longer one, and it is how you reach Hai Van Gate.

The town is small. Đường Nguyễn Văn, along Lap An, is the evening if the walking nights are still running. The 2024 trial was Friday, Saturday, and Sunday evenings and was explicitly subject to change. No 2026 calendar was opened, so ask locally. Tân Cảnh Dương is the livelier beach in the same zone, with bars and a seafood fire in the Visit Hue note. It is not a separate town. Chân Mây is the port in the 2018 plan, not a second swimming beach.
gettingAround: Highway 1A runs beside the beach. Nguyễn Văn runs along the lagoon. One paper describes the walking segment as about 450 m from the new market toward Trường THCS Lăng Cô. A taxi, a hired car, or a motorbike covers the station, the beach, and the lagoon.

Phu Bai is the nearest airport. The national page says Lang Co is about 40 km from it, and that figure is that page only. The heritage trains between Hue and Da Nang list Ga Lăng Cô. The same operator page prints two clocks, and the lower boxes leave about 10 minutes at the stop. Use the ticket. Do not assume a north–south SE train stops here.

Hai Van Gate is up the pass road, not through the tunnel. Tân Cảnh Dương and Chân Mây are the north side of the same zone. Bach Ma is the cloud forest above the lagoon. From the park’s 25 Dec 2025 notice, vehicles stop at the km 12 slip from 1 Jan 2026. Be at the visitor center before 09:00 and back before 17:00.

stayAreas.name: The bay strip
stayAreas.summary: Sleep here if the morning you want is the sand and the ridge. The national page and Visit Hue both describe stays on this shore and do not name a brand as the reason to come.

stayAreas.name: South side of Lap An
stayAreas.summary: The 2018 tourism-zone plan puts lower hotels on the south side of the lagoon. It is the land side of the same town, not a second beach.

eat: Lap An oysters are the local plate: grilled over a fire, in porridge, stir-fried with onion, or as a salad. Báo Quốc Tế says the lagoon has raised them since the late 1990s, and you eat them with the boats and the stakes in view.
Grilled seafood is the evening at Tân Cảnh Dương, on the beach, as Visit Hue describes it. Visit Hue does not name a shop or a species list. Nguyễn Văn has long had specialty stalls along the lagoon.
interestsBody: Oysters are the lagoon. The swim is the bay under the pass. The sand strip across Lap An shows only at a strong low tide.
Hai Van Gate is the look back at that bay, on the pass road. The tunnel does not pass the gate.

interestGroups.title: Dining and F&B
interestGroups.summary: Lap An oysters, the lagoon shellfish, and the grill at Tan Canh Duong.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: Oysters on Đầm Lập An, the shellfish Nhân Dân names, and grilled seafood in the evening at Tân Cảnh Dương.

interestGroups.title: Oysters on Lap An
interestGroups.summary: The brackish lagoon between Phu Gia and the bay is where Lang Co raises and serves oysters.
body: Đầm Lập An sits beside Highway 1A at đèo Phú Gia, with the Bach Ma range on one side and the bay on the other. Báo Quốc Tế says oyster farming here dates from the late 1990s. You eat on the lagoon, with the boats and the stakes in view, not from a ranked restaurant list.

The preparations that paper names are hàu nướng trui, cháo hàu, hàu xào hành tây, and gỏi hàu. No stall price was printed. A household raft feature is not a town ticket. March to June is that paper’s best-looking months for the lagoon, and it is not a harvest calendar.

cards.title: Lap An Lagoon
cards.summary: Look from the shore or from Nguyễn Văn. Oyster stakes and round boats are the working landscape.

interestGroups.title: The bay under the pass
interestGroups.summary: The swim is a long curve under Hai Van, between Hue and Da Nang, not a city beach.
body: The national beach page describes about 10 km of gentle shore, white sand, and clear water, beside Highway 1A under the pass. Visit Hue calls the same bay a resort beach, not a city promenade. Neither page prints a beach ticket.
Come in the morning or late afternoon if you want the ridge in the light. Visit Hue names summer for the swim. The national page gives a summer average around 25°C.
Hue is about 60 km north if the citadel is the trip. Da Nang is about 25 km through the tunnel, on the national page only, if the city beach is the trip.

cards.title: Lang Co Beach
cards.summary: Swim and walk the curve. No beach ticket was printed. The ridge should stay in the frame.

interestGroups.title: The sand bridge
interestGroups.summary: At a strong low tide, Lap An shows a sand strip the local paper calls cây cầu cát.
body: Báo Quốc Tế describes a tide-built sand bridge across Đầm Lập An, and it says the strip is short and easy to miss. It shows only at a strong low tide. Do not start across it as the tide turns.
The lagoon and the bay are not the same water, and Đầm An Cư, at the foot of the pass, is a different lagoon on the economic-zone page. This card is the strip on Lap An.

cards.title: The strip at low tide
cards.summary: A pale sand strip on Lap An, with the mountain behind it. Go at a strong low tide, and turn back before the water returns.

interestGroups.title: Hai Van gate
interestGroups.summary: The 1826 gate on the pass is the lookout back onto this bay, and it is the south edge of the tourism zone.
body: Hải Vân Quan stands above 500 m on the Hue–Da Nang boundary. It was built in 1826 under Minh Mạng as the southern gate of the capital. Visitors have been allowed in since 1 Aug 2024, after restoration. Both cities manage it.

From 2 June 2026 the fee is 70,000 VND per person per visit, the same for domestic and international visitors, through 31 Dec 2028. VTV and VnExpress both report that figure from the Hue monuments center. VnExpress also prints 07:00–17:30 and a free entry under 1.2 m. Check the board.
The gate is on the pass road. The tunnel is the shorter way between Da Nang and Lang Co, and it does not pass the gate.

cards.title: Hai Van Gate
cards.summary: Walk the restored gate and look back at the bay. 70,000 VND from 2 June 2026. The tunnel does not stop here.

interestGroups.title: Shopping
interestGroups.summary: Chợ Lăng Cô and the stalls along Nguyễn Văn.

cards.title: Shopping
cards.summary: The town market, and the lagoon stalls on Nguyễn Văn.

season.label: Summer for the swim
season.note: Visit Hue names summer for these beaches. The national page gives a summer average around 25°C. Báo Quốc Tế calls March to June the best-looking months on Lap An, and that line is one paper. A closure calendar for the pass, the tunnel, or Highway 1A was not opened. Cầu ngư and the boat race are on the morning of mùng 6 Tết at làng An Cư Đông. The civil date moves. No ticket was printed.

faqs.q: Should you stay in Lang Co or in Hue?
faqs.a: Stay in Lang Co if the morning you want is this bay. Hue is about 60 km north, and the citadel is a separate day.

faqs.q: Does the Hai Van tunnel stop at the gate?
faqs.a: No. The national page says the tunnel is the shorter road, about 25 km from Da Nang, and the pass road is the longer one that reaches Hải Vân Quan. The 25 km figure is that page only.

faqs.q: Is there a ticket for Lang Co beach?
faqs.a: Neither the national beach page nor Visit Hue prints a beach ticket. if a gate asks. Hải Vân Quan is a separate fee, 70,000 VND from 2 June 2026.

faqs.q: When is the Lang Co boat race?
faqs.a: On the morning of mùng 6 Tết at làng An Cư Đông, described as yearly. The civil date moves. The 2026 and 2027 dates were not printed. No ticket was printed.
